change.title: fix(web): probe held sockets, wait to confirm lost prompts and tier transcript flushes
change.description: ## Summary A phone or browser client has several reconnect and prompt-retry problems. A tab that returns from the background closes a socket that the host still holds. A stalled handshake can wait one minute. A prompt whose reply is lost shows as failed, although the host accepted it. Long streamed code blocks make the chat slow. This PR fixes the client side of these problems. It builds on the host change in #1076. ## Related Issue Closes #1065 No duplicate PR exists. This PR completes the work that #1076 started. ## Type of Change - [ ] feat: new feature - [x] fix: bug fix - [ ] docs: documentation only - [ ] style: formatting or non-functional styling changes - [ ] refactor: internal cleanup with no behavior change - [ ] perf: performance improvement - [ ] test: adds or updates tests - [ ] build: build or dependency changes - [ ] ci: CI/CD workflow changes - [ ] chore: maintenance or tooling - [ ] revert: reverts a previous change ## What Changed - A client that returns from the background now sends a ping on the held `/ws` socket. It reconnects only if the ping fails. The forced reconnect after 30 seconds hidden is removed. A plain window focus on a socket that never left no longer sends a ping. - Each socket (`/ws`, `/terminal/ws` and the persistence socket) now fails a stalled handshake after about 10 seconds. - Reconnect backoff is exponential with 25 % jitter. The attempt counter resets only after 60 seconds of stable connection. Wake, online, visibility and focus events cut a pending backoff short. - Request timers now depend on the request type. They are never shorter than the host limit (an agent install gets 330 seconds). - One failing session during a resubscribe now retries alone. The socket and the other sessions stay up. - A terminal re-attach that times out on an open socket now recycles the connection. Typed input is no longer lost. - A prompt whose reply is lost now stays open with a "Waiting to confirm..." notice. The client resends the same `turnId` after the reconnect. The host answers with a receipt. Only an explicit host error fails the prompt. The old "fail on unknown outcome" path is removed. Stop cancels a pending resend, including one already in flight. - The chat treats the new `error`, `timeout` and `crashed` stop reasons as the end of a turn. - Transcript flushes now use tiers. The watched session flushes at most every 30 ms on `requestAnimationFrame`. Background sessions flush every 100 ms. Approvals and questions flush at once. Every session flushes on `visibilitychange`. The 250 ms backstop stays. - Stream-storm measurement: a 3200-line open code block was highlighted in full on every update (347 highlighter calls, 36 million highlighted characters, about 5 seconds per call at the end). An open block larger than 8000 characters now shows as plain text. It is highlighted once when it closes. The test run now shows 13 calls and 0.3 times the block size. - Host test fixes that came out of review: a terminal attach count can no longer leak when an attach fails or is cancelled. A new test runs the real command loop through a process shutdown. ## How It Was Tested - [x] `bun run ci` (Biome lint + format + imports, strict mode) - [x] `bun run typecheck` - [x] `bun run test` - [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` (in src-tauri) - [x] `cargo test` (in src-tauri) - [x] Manual verification completed - [ ] Not applicable New tests use fake timers and a fake WebSocket. They cover the probe, the handshake timers, jitter and the 60 second reset, per-type timers, the per-session retry, the terminal re-attach, the pending-confirm resend and Stop, the flush tiers and the open code block. I made the screenshot with a headless browser against a built web client and a test server. A wrapper dropped the socket on the first prompt. ## Screenshots or Recordings The prompt stays in the transcript. A "Waiting to confirm..." notice shows above the composer. No error banner shows. ![Waiting to confirm state at 1440x900, dark theme](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/gnoviawan/e126207113a2181eb182b35e75e4b4ef/raw/waiting-to-confirm.png) ## CI & Review Gate - [ ] All CI checks pass (PR Validation, Rust Checks, Build Verification, Security Scans) - [ ] Code review comments from CodeRabbit / Claude have been addressed or resolved - [ ] No unresolved review findings remain ## Checklist - [x] My PR title follows the conventional commit format used by this repo - [x] I linked the related issue or explained why none exists - [x] I updated docs when needed - [x] I added or updated tests when needed - [x] I verified the change does not introduce unrelated modifications - [x] I read AGENTS.md and followed the contributor guidelines - [ ] A human reviewed the complete diff before submission --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes client-side transport and prompt tracking. A tab returning from the background now pings the held `/ws` socket and reconnects only if the probe fails — the forced reconnect after 30s hidden is gone — handshakes time out after ~10s, and a prompt whose reply was lost stays open with a "Waiting to confirm…" state instead of failing, resending the same `turnId` until the host answers with a receipt (closes #1065; builds on the host change in #1076). **Socket transport** - Reconnect backoff is exponential with ±25% jitter and resets only after 60s of stable connection; wake, online, visibility, and focus events cut a pending backoff short. - Request timers are per request type and never shorter than the host's bound. - One failing session resubscribe now retries alone; the socket and other sessions stay up. - A terminal re-attach that times out on an open socket recycles the connection, and failed or cancelled attaches release their attachment counts. **Prompt tracking and rendering** - A lost prompt reply keeps the turn open in a pending-confirm state; only an explicit host error fails it, and Stop cancels pending resends (including one in flight). Queued prompts flush after a late terminator and per-session pending state clears once a turn settles. New stop reasons `error`, `timeout`, and `crashed` end a turn. - Transcript flushes are tiered: the watched session flushes on `requestAnimationFrame` (≤30ms), background sessions every 100ms, approvals and questions immediately, everything on `visibilitychange`; the 250ms backstop stays. - Open code blocks over 8000 characters render as plain text while streaming and highlight once when the fence closes, avoiding re-highlighting the whole block on every update. Written for commit 160cc6988dfb1fcbab38177c5ce00717a4169e47. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved recovery from connection drops, including more reliable reconnects, session restoration, and prompt resubmission. * Added clearer feedback when a prompt is awaiting confirmation and when a turn ends with an error. * Fixed terminal reconnection handling to prevent failed or interrupted attachments from lingering. * Improved chat transcript responsiveness and reduced highlighting delays for long, unfinished code blocks.

+import { code as shikiCodePlugin } from '@streamdown/code'
+import type { CodeHighlighterPlugin } from 'streamdown'
+
+/** Languages that carry no grammar: highlighting them only tokenizes and caches. */
+const PLAIN_TEXT_LANGUAGES = new Set(['text', 'txt', 'plain', 'plaintext'])
+
+/**
+ * Shiki code plugin for chat fences, with one change: plain-text blocks skip
+ * the highlighter and render Streamdown's unhighlighted fallback. `ChatMarkdownCode`
+ * hands an open, oversized fence to Streamdown as `text` so the stream does not
+ * re-tokenize (and cache) the whole growing fence on every commit; the real
+ * language is applied once the fence closes.
+ */
+export const chatCodePlugin: CodeHighlighterPlugin = {
+  ...shikiCodePlugin,
+  highlight(options, callback) {
+    if (PLAIN_TEXT_LANGUAGES.has(options.language.trim().toLowerCase())) return null
+    return shikiCodePlugin.highlight(options, callback)
+  }
+}

+import { code as shikiCodePlugin } from '@streamdown/code'
+import { act, render, waitFor } from '@testing-library/react'

+import { ChatMarkdownCode, OPEN_FENCE_HIGHLIGHT_MAX_CHARS } from './chat-markdown-code'
+
+function fenceBody(lines: number): string {
+  return Array.from(
+    { length: lines },
+    (_, i) => `const value${i} = compute(${i}) // line ${i}`
+  ).join('\n')
+}
+
+function renderChat(text: string, streaming: boolean) {
+  const ui = (value: string, isStreaming: boolean) => (
+    <TooltipProvider>
+      <Streamdown
+        mode={isStreaming ? 'streaming' : 'static'}
+        isAnimating={isStreaming}
+        parseIncompleteMarkdown={isStreaming}
+        plugins={{ code: chatCodePlugin }}
+        components={{ code: ChatMarkdownCode }}
+        controls={false}
+        lineNumbers={false}
+        linkSafety={{ enabled: false }}
+      >
+        {value}
+      </Streamdown>
+    </TooltipProvider>
+  )
+  const view = render(ui(text, streaming))
+  return {
+    ...view,
+    update: (value: string, isStreaming: boolean) => view.rerender(ui(value, isStreaming))
+  }
+}
+
+describe('streaming code fences', () => {
+  afterEach(() => vi.restoreAllMocks())
+
+  it('never highlights a partial oversized open fence across stream ticks, then highlights the full body once at close', async () => {
+    const highlight = vi.spyOn(shikiCodePlugin, 'highlight')
+    const body = fenceBody(Math.ceil(OPEN_FENCE_HIGHLIGHT_MAX_CHARS / 40) + 40)
+    expect(body.length).toBeGreaterThan(OPEN_FENCE_HIGHLIGHT_MAX_CHARS)
+    // Every stage is already past the live-highlight bound.
+    const first = Math.floor(OPEN_FENCE_HIGHLIGHT_MAX_CHARS * 1.1)
+    expect(first).toBeLessThan(body.length)
+
+    // Let each commit settle through React's effects and any async highlight
+    // scheduling before the next tokens arrive.
+    const settle = () => act(async () => new Promise<void>((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 150)))
+
+    const view = renderChat(`\`\`\`ts\n${body.slice(0, first)}`, true)
+    await settle()
+    const stages = [
+      first,
+      ...[0.5, 0.7, 0.85, 1].map((f) => Math.floor(first + (body.length - first) * f))
+    ]
+    for (const end of stages.slice(1)) {
+      view.update(`\`\`\`ts\n${body.slice(0, end)}`, true)
+      await settle()
+    }
+    // Several commits of a still-open, oversized fence: the highlighter never
+    // saw any (partial) source of it.
+    expect(highlight.mock.calls.map(([options]) => options.code.length)).toEqual([])
+    expect(
+      view.container.querySelector('[data-streamdown="code-block-body"]')?.textContent
+    ).toContain('line 0')
+
+    // The fence closes and the message settles: exactly the full body, once.
+    view.update(`\`\`\`ts\n${body}\n\`\`\``, false)
+    await waitFor(() => expect(highlight).toHaveBeenCalled(), { timeout: 15_000 })
+    await settle()
+    expect(highlight).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)
+    const [options] = highlight.mock.calls[0]
+    expect(options.language).toBe('ts')
+    expect(options.code).toBe(body)
+  }, 30_000)
+
+  it('AgentProse (the real chat renderer) never highlights a partial oversized open fence, then highlights the full body once at close', async () => {
+    const highlight = vi.spyOn(shikiCodePlugin, 'highlight')
+    const body = fenceBody(Math.ceil(OPEN_FENCE_HIGHLIGHT_MAX_CHARS / 40) + 40)
+    const first = Math.floor(OPEN_FENCE_HIGHLIGHT_MAX_CHARS * 1.1)
+    // The streaming text is throttled (10 Hz trailing edge): settle past it.
+    const settle = () => act(async () => new Promise<void>((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 250)))
+    const ui = (value: string, streaming: boolean) => (
+      <TooltipProvider>
+        <AgentProse text={value} streaming={streaming} reduced />
+      </TooltipProvider>
+    )
+
+    const view = render(ui(`\`\`\`ts\n${body.slice(0, first)}`, true))
+    await settle()
+    for (const f of [0.5, 0.7, 0.85, 1]) {
+      const end = Math.floor(first + (body.length - first) * f)
+      view.rerender(ui(`\`\`\`ts\n${body.slice(0, end)}`, true))
+      await settle()
+    }
+    expect(highlight.mock.calls.map(([options]) => options.code.length)).toEqual([])
+    expect(
+      view.container.querySelector('[data-streamdown="code-block-body"]')?.textContent
+    ).toContain('line 0')
+
+    view.rerender(ui(`\`\`\`ts\n${body}\n\`\`\``, false))
+    await waitFor(() => expect(highlight).toHaveBeenCalled(), { timeout: 15_000 })
+    await settle()
+    expect(highlight).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)
+    const [options] = highlight.mock.calls[0]
+    expect(options.language).toBe('ts')
+    expect(options.code).toBe(body)
+  }, 30_000)
+
+  it('keeps live highlighting for a small open fence', async () => {
+    const highlight = vi.spyOn(shikiCodePlugin, 'highlight')
+    renderChat(`\`\`\`ts\n${fenceBody(5)}`, true)
+    await waitFor(() => expect(highlight).toHaveBeenCalled(), { timeout: 15_000 })
+    expect(highlight.mock.calls[0][0].language).toBe('ts')
+  })
+})
+
+describe('chatCodePlugin', () => {
+  it.each(['text', 'TXT', 'plaintext'])('skips the highlighter for %s blocks', (language) => {
+    const highlight = vi.spyOn(shikiCodePlugin, 'highlight')
+    const callback = vi.fn()
+    expect(
+      chatCodePlugin.highlight(
+        { code: 'a', language, themes: ['github-light', 'github-dark'] },
+        callback
+      )
+    ).toBeNull()
+    expect(highlight).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
+    expect(callback).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
+    highlight.mockRestore()
+  })
+})

+/**
+ * Per-session resubscribe retry (CLI-F1). After a reconnect, one session whose
+ * `subscribe` fails must NOT tear the socket down or hold back the other
+ * sessions: it is retried alone with its own bounded, jittered backoff.
+ *
+ * The first {@link SESSION_CURSOR_RETRY_ATTEMPTS} retries replay from the cursor
+ * again (the failure may be transient); later attempts degrade the session to
+ * snapshot + live (ARCHITECTURE-SPINE Conventions › Degradation). After
+ * {@link SESSION_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS} the session is handed back via `onGiveUp`.
+ */
+import { jitteredBackoffMs } from './ws-transport-timing'
+
+export const SESSION_RETRY_BASE_MS = 1_000
+export const SESSION_RETRY_MAX_MS = 30_000
+export const SESSION_CURSOR_RETRY_ATTEMPTS = 2
+export const SESSION_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 6
+
+export type SessionRetryMode = 'cursor' | 'degrade'
+
+interface RetryEntry {
+  attempt: number
+  timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null
+}
+
+export class SessionResubscribeRetry {
+  private readonly entries = new Map<string, RetryEntry>()
+
+  constructor(
+    private readonly deps: {
+      /** One retry attempt; reject to schedule the next one. */
+      run: (sessionId: string, mode: SessionRetryMode) => Promise<void>
+      /** The retry budget is exhausted. */
+      onGiveUp: (sessionId: string, lastError: unknown) => void
+      /** False while the socket is not authenticated + OPEN (the reconnect pass owns recovery). */
+      canRun: () => boolean
+      random?: () => number
+    }
+  ) {}
+
+  has(sessionId: string): boolean {
+    return this.entries.has(sessionId)
+  }
+
+  /** Arm (or advance) the retry for `sessionId`; a pending timer is left alone. */
+  schedule(sessionId: string, lastError?: unknown): void {
+    const entry = this.entries.get(sessionId) ?? { attempt: 0, timer: null }
+    if (entry.timer) return
+    if (entry.attempt >= SESSION_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS) {
+      this.entries.delete(sessionId)
+      this.deps.onGiveUp(sessionId, lastError)
+      return
+    }
+    const delay = jitteredBackoffMs(
+      entry.attempt,
+      SESSION_RETRY_BASE_MS,
+      SESSION_RETRY_MAX_MS,
+      this.deps.random
+    )
+    entry.attempt += 1
+    entry.timer = setTimeout(() => {
+      entry.timer = null
+      void this.fire(sessionId, entry)
+    }, delay)
+    this.entries.set(sessionId, entry)
+  }
+
+  cancel(sessionId: string): void {
+    const entry = this.entries.get(sessionId)
+    if (entry?.timer) clearTimeout(entry.timer)
+    this.entries.delete(sessionId)
+  }
+
+  cancelAll(): void {
+    for (const entry of this.entries.values()) {
+      if (entry.timer) clearTimeout(entry.timer)
+    }
+    this.entries.clear()
+  }
+
+  private async fire(sessionId: string, entry: RetryEntry): Promise<void> {
+    if (this.entries.get(sessionId) !== entry) return
+    if (!this.deps.canRun()) {
+      // The socket is not live right now (a reconnect pass is running or
+      // about to run). Keep the entry and re-arm — bounded by the same
+      // attempt budget — instead of silently dropping the session: if the
+      // reconnect pass takes it over, its `cancelAll`/`cancel` removes this
+      // entry first; if it never does, the budget ends in `onGiveUp`.
+      this.schedule(sessionId, new Error('socket not live when the retry fired'))
+      return
+    }
+    const mode: SessionRetryMode =
+      entry.attempt <= SESSION_CURSOR_RETRY_ATTEMPTS ? 'cursor' : 'degrade'
+    try {
+      await this.deps.run(sessionId, mode)
+      if (this.entries.get(sessionId) === entry) this.entries.delete(sessionId)
+    } catch (err) {
+      if (this.entries.get(sessionId) !== entry) return
+      this.schedule(sessionId, err)
+    }
+  }
+}

+ * `/terminal/ws`, the persistence socket): handshake bound, reconnect
+ * backoff with jitter, and per-request-type timers.
+ *
+ * Design rules (ARCHITECTURE-SPINE Conventions › Reconnect):
+ * - every socket has its own ~10 s handshake timeout (upgrade + authenticate);
+ * - reconnect backoff is exponential with ±25 % jitter and the attempt counter
+ *   resets only after the connection has been stable for 60 s;
+ * - request timers are per request type and never shorter than the host's own
+ *   bound for that type.
+ */

+
+/** Generic request timer for host operations that answer promptly. */
+export const REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000
+
+/** Upgrade + `authenticate` budget for every socket the client opens. */
+export const HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000
+
+export const RECONNECT_BASE_MS = 500
+export const RECONNECT_MAX_MS = 8_000
+/** Backoff delay is scaled by a uniform factor in `1 ± RECONNECT_JITTER_RATIO`. */
+export const RECONNECT_JITTER_RATIO = 0.25
+/** The attempt counter resets only after the connection stayed up this long. */
+export const RECONNECT_STABLE_MS = 60_000
+/** Minimum spacing between wake-triggered early reconnect attempts. */
+export const RECONNECT_EXPEDITE_MIN_INTERVAL_MS = 1_000

+ * for tests (`() => 0` → lower bound, `() => 1` → upper bound).

+  attempt: number,
+  baseMs: number = RECONNECT_BASE_MS,
+  maxMs: number = RECONNECT_MAX_MS,

+  const factor = 1 + (random() * 2 - 1) * RECONNECT_JITTER_RATIO

+/**
+ * Tiered flush clock for the transcript coalescing buffer (Conventions ›
+ * Render clocks):
+ *
+ * - the WATCHED session (the one on screen) flushes at most every
+ *   {@link WATCHED_FLUSH_MS} on `requestAnimationFrame`;
+ * - every BACKGROUND session flushes on a {@link BACKGROUND_FLUSH_MS} timer;
+ * - the {@link FLUSH_BACKSTOP_MS} timer drains everything when rAF is
+ *   suspended (an occluded/minimized WebView keeps the callback armed but never
+ *   fires it — without it a hidden-but-streaming session buffers unboundedly);
+ * - approvals/questions and `visibilitychange` flush immediately through the
+ *   owner's `flushNow` (see `transcript.ts`), which also cancels this clock.
+ *
+ * The clock owns scheduling only: what is buffered, and how a flush applies it,
+ * stays with the host.
+ */
+
+export type FlushTier = 'watched' | 'background' | 'all'
+
+export const WATCHED_FLUSH_MS = 30
+export const BACKGROUND_FLUSH_MS = 100
+export const FLUSH_BACKSTOP_MS = 250
+
+export interface FlushClockHost {
+  /** True while `sessionId` is the session on screen. Re-evaluated at fire time. */
+  isWatched: (sessionId: string) => boolean
+  /** Apply and remove the buffered updates of `tier`. */
+  flush: (tier: FlushTier) => void
+  /** True while buffered updates of `tier` remain. */
+  hasPending: (tier: FlushTier) => boolean
+}
+
+export interface FlushClock {
+  /** An update for `sessionId` was buffered: arm the clock for its tier. */
+  note: (sessionId: string) => void
+  /** Cancel every armed timer/frame (the owner is flushing synchronously). */
+  cancel: () => void
+  /** True while any frame or timer is armed. */
+  isArmed: () => boolean
+}
+
+export function createFlushClock(host: FlushClockHost): FlushClock {
+  let rafId: number | null = null
+  let watchedTimerId: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined
+  let backgroundTimerId: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined
+  let backstopTimerId: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined
+  let lastWatchedFlushAt = Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY
+
+  const hasRaf = (): boolean => typeof requestAnimationFrame === 'function'
+  const nowMs = (): number => performance.now()
+
+  function cancelWatched(): void {
+    if (rafId !== null) {
+      cancelAnimationFrame(rafId)
+      rafId = null
+    }
+    clearTimeout(watchedTimerId)
+    watchedTimerId = undefined
+  }
+
+  function cancelBackground(): void {
+    clearTimeout(backgroundTimerId)
+    backgroundTimerId = undefined
+  }
+
+  function cancelBackstop(): void {
+    clearTimeout(backstopTimerId)
+    backstopTimerId = undefined
+  }
+
+  function cancel(): void {
+    cancelWatched()
+    cancelBackground()
+    cancelBackstop()
+  }
+
+  /** Re-arm whatever the buffer still needs after any flush; drop the rest. */
+  function rearm(): void {
+    if (host.hasPending('watched')) armWatched()
+    else cancelWatched()
+    if (host.hasPending('background')) armBackground()
+    else cancelBackground()
+    if (host.hasPending('all')) armBackstop()
+    else cancelBackstop()
+  }
+
+  function runFlush(tier: FlushTier): void {
+    if (tier === 'all') cancel()
+    else if (tier === 'watched') cancelWatched()
+    else cancelBackground()
+    if (tier !== 'background') lastWatchedFlushAt = nowMs()
+    host.flush(tier)
+    rearm()
+  }
+
+  function onFrame(): void {
+    rafId = null
+    // ≥ 30 ms since the last watched flush, else wait for another frame.

+      rafId = requestAnimationFrame(onFrame)
+      return
+    }
+    runFlush('watched')

+    if (rafId !== null || watchedTimerId !== undefined) return
+    if (hasRaf()) {
+      rafId = requestAnimationFrame(onFrame)
+    } else {
+      // No rAF (non-browser host): replicate the cadence with a timer.
+      const wait = Math.max(0, lastWatchedFlushAt + WATCHED_FLUSH_MS - nowMs())
+      watchedTimerId = setTimeout(() => {
+        watchedTimerId = undefined
+        runFlush('watched')
+      }, wait)
+    }
+  }

+    if (backgroundTimerId !== undefined) return
+    backgroundTimerId = setTimeout(() => {
+      backgroundTimerId = undefined
+      runFlush('background')
+    }, BACKGROUND_FLUSH_MS)
+  }
+
+  function armBackstop(): void {
+    if (backstopTimerId !== undefined) return
+    backstopTimerId = setTimeout(() => {
+      backstopTimerId = undefined
+      runFlush('all')
+    }, FLUSH_BACKSTOP_MS)
+  }
+
+  return {
+    note(sessionId) {

+    },
+    cancel,
+    isArmed: () =>

+      watchedTimerId !== undefined ||

+  }
+}
